section: Science · Ch45 — Methodology of Teaching Science
subject: Science
stem: A teacher asks pupils to observe a burning candle, form a guess about why the flame changes colour, and then test that guess with a simple experiment. This approach chiefly develops:

options.option_text: Scientific temper and the process skills of observation, hypothesis and experimentation
Rote memorisation of facts about candles
Handwriting skills only
Artistic drawing ability

explanation: This inquiry-based sequence (observe → hypothesise → test) builds scientific temper and process skills, the central aim of science teaching under NCF 2005, rather than mere fact recall.

section: Science · Ch45 — Methodology of Teaching Science
subject: Science
stem: In the laboratory (experimental) method of teaching science, the primary role of the pupil is to:

options.option_text: Perform experiments individually or in small groups to discover facts first-hand
Only watch the teacher perform every experiment
Memorise the textbook diagrams without any hands-on work
Copy the experiment's conclusion from the blackboard

explanation: The laboratory method is learner-centred: pupils themselves manipulate apparatus and observe outcomes, building first-hand understanding — distinct from the teacher-centred demonstration method, where the teacher alone performs the experiment.

section: Science · Ch45 — Methodology of Teaching Science
subject: Science
stem: When apparatus is costly, scarce, or dangerous for pupils to handle directly (e.g. a experiment requiring an open flame in a young class), the most suitable method is:

options.option_text: Demonstration method
Individual laboratory method for every child
Project method spread over weeks
Pure lecture with no visual aid at all

explanation: The demonstration method lets the teacher safely perform an experiment for the whole class to observe — appropriate when equipment is limited, costly, or hazardous for direct pupil handling.

section: Science · Ch45 — Methodology of Teaching Science
subject: Science
stem: A class spends three weeks growing and observing bean plants under different watering conditions, then presents findings as a group report. This is an example of the:

options.option_text: Project method
Lecture method
Demonstration method (teacher-led only)
Drill and practice method

explanation: The project method involves pupils in an extended, purposeful, real-life activity (growing plants over weeks) culminating in a concrete outcome/report — associated with Kilpatrick, building on Dewey's 'learning by doing'.

section: Science · Ch45 — Methodology of Teaching Science
subject: Science
stem: Organising an annual school Science Fair, where students display self-made working models and experiments, primarily helps to develop pupils':

options.option_text: Creativity, application of concepts, and communication of scientific ideas
Ability to memorise textbook definitions verbatim
Skill in copying answers from reference guides
Speed in solving objective-type test papers

explanation: Science fairs encourage students to apply concepts creatively into working models and to explain/defend their reasoning — developing application and communication skills beyond rote recall or test-taking speed.
